title: अंश ५ · अध्याय २६

items.text:
भीष्मकः कुणिडने राजा विदर्भविषयेऽभवत् ।
रूकमी तस्याभवत् पुत्रो रुविमणी च वराङ्गन ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
bhīṣmakaḥ kuṇiḍane rājā vidarbhaviṣaye'bhavat |
rūkamī tasyābhavat putro ruvimaṇī ca varāṅgana || 1 ||

items.text:
रुक्मिणी चकमे कृष्णः सा च तं चारुहासिनी ।
नि ददौ याचते चैनां रुक्मी द्रेषेण चक्रिणो ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
rukmiṇī cakame kṛṣṇaḥ sā ca taṃ cāruhāsinī |
ni dadau yācate caināṃ rukmī dreṣeṇa cakriṇo || 2 ||

items.text:
ददौ च शिशुपालाय जरासन्धप्रदेशितः ।
भीष्मको रुक्मिणा सार्द्ध रुक्मिणीमुरुविक्रमः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
dadau ca śiśupālāya jarāsandhapradeśitaḥ |
bhīṣmako rukmiṇā sārddha rukmiṇīmuruvikramaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
विवाहार्थं ततः सर्व्वे जरासन्धमुखा नृपाः ।
भीष्मकस्य पुरं जग्मुः शिशुपालप्रियैषिणः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
vivāhārthaṃ tataḥ sarvve jarāsandhamukhā nṛpāḥ |
bhīṣmakasya puraṃ jagmuḥ śiśupālapriyaiṣiṇaḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
कृष्णोऽपि बलभद्राद्यर्यादवैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।
प्रययौ कुण्दिनं द्रष्टुं विवाहञ्चैव भूभृतः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
kṛṣṇo'pi balabhadrādyaryādavairbahubhirvṛtaḥ |
prayayau kuṇdinaṃ draṣṭuṃ vivāhañcaiva bhūbhṛtaḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
शोभाविनि विवाहे तु तां कन्यां ह्टतवान् हरिः ।
विपक्षभारमासज्य रामाद्य ष्वथ बन्धुषु ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
śobhāvini vivāhe tu tāṃ kanyāṃ hṭatavān hariḥ |
vipakṣabhāramāsajya rāmādya ṣvatha bandhuṣu || 6 ||

items.text:
ततश्व पौण्ड्रकः श्रीमान् दन्तवक्रो विदूरथः ।
शिशुपाल-जरासन्ध-शाल्वाद्याश्व महीभृतः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tataśva pauṇḍrakaḥ śrīmān dantavakro vidūrathaḥ |
śiśupāla-jarāsandha-śālvādyāśva mahībhṛtaḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
कुपितास्ते हरिं हन्तुं चक्रु रुदूयोगमुत्तमम् ।
निर्ज्जिताश्व समागम्य रामाद्यर्यदुपुङ्गवैः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
kupitāste hariṃ hantuṃ cakru rudūyogamuttamam |
nirjjitāśva samāgamya rāmādyaryadupuṅgavaiḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
कुणिडनं न प्रवेक्ष्यामि अहत्वा युधि केशवम् ।
कृत्वा प्रतिज्ञां रुकमी च हन्तुं कृष्णमभिद्रुतः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
kuṇiḍanaṃ na pravekṣyāmi ahatvā yudhi keśavam |
kṛtvā pratijñāṃ rukamī ca hantuṃ kṛṣṇamabhidrutaḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
हत्वा बलं सनागाश्व-पत्ति-स्यन्दनसङ्कुलम् ।
निर्जितः पातितश्वोर्व्व्यां लीलयैव स चकिणा ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
hatvā balaṃ sanāgāśva-patti-syandanasaṅkulam |
nirjitaḥ pātitaśvorvvyāṃ līlayaiva sa cakiṇā || 10 ||

items.text:
हन्तु कृतमतिः कृष्णो रुक्मिणां युद्धदुर्म्मदम् ।
प्रणम्य याचितो ब्रह्मन् रुविमण्या मगवान हरिः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
hantu kṛtamatiḥ kṛṣṇo rukmiṇāṃ yuddhadurmmadam |
praṇamya yācito brahman ruvimaṇyā magavāna hariḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
एक एव मम भ्राता न हन्तव्यस्त्वयाधुना ।
कोपं नियम्य देवेश!भ्रातृभिक्षा प्रदीयताम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
eka eva mama bhrātā na hantavyastvayādhunā |
kopaṃ niyamya deveśa!bhrātṛbhikṣā pradīyatām || 12 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्तेन परित्यक्तः कृष्णेनाक्लिष्टकर्म्मणा ।
रुक्मी भोजकटं नाम पुरं कुत्वावसत् तदा ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktena parityaktaḥ kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmmaṇā |
rukmī bhojakaṭaṃ nāma puraṃ kutvāvasat tadā || 13 ||

items.text:
निर्जित्य रुक्मिणं सम्यगुपयेमे स रुक्मिणीम् ।
राक्षसेन विवाहेन सम्प्रप्तां मधुसूदनः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
nirjitya rukmiṇaṃ samyagupayeme sa rukmiṇīm |
rākṣasena vivāhena sampraptāṃ madhusūdanaḥ || 14 ||

items.text:
तस्यां जज्ञ ऽथ प्रद्युम्रो मदनांश- स वीर्य्यवान् ।
जहार शम्बरो यं वै यो जघान च शम्बरम् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tasyāṃ jajña 'tha pradyumro madanāṃśa- sa vīryyavān |
jahāra śambaro yaṃ vai yo jaghāna ca śambaram || 15 ||

en_chapter: Bhishmaka was king of Vidarbha, residing at Kundina. He had a son named Rukmin, and a beautiful daughter termed Rukmini. Krishna fell in love with the latter, and solicited her in marriage: but her brother who hated Krishna, would not assent to the espousals. At the suggestion of Jarāsandha, and with the concurrence of his son, the powerful sovereign Bhishmaka affianced Rukmini to Sisupāla. In order to celebrate the nuptials, Jarāsandha and other princes, the friends of Sisupāla, assembled in the capital of Vidharba; and Krishna, attended by Balabhadra and many other Yādavas, also went to Kundina to witness the wedding. When there, Hari contrived on the eve of the nuptials, to carry off the princess, leaving Rāma and his kinsmen to sustain the weight of his enemies. Paundraka, the illustrious Dantavakra, Viduratha, Sisupāla, Jarāsandha, Salya, and other kings, indignant at the insult, exerted themselves to kill Krishna, but were repelled by Balarāma and the Yādavas. Rukmin, vowing that he would never enter Kundina again until he had slain Kesava in fight, pursued and overtook him. In the combat that ensued, Krishna destroyed with his discus, as if in sport the host of Rukmin, with all its horses, and elephants, and foot, and chariots, and overthrew him, and hurled him on the ground; and would have put him to death, but was withheld by the entreaties of Rukmini. "He is my only brother," she exclaimed, "and must not be slain by thee; restrain your wrath, O divine Lord, and give me my brother in charity".

Thus addressed by her, Krishna, whom no acts affect, spared Rukmin; and he (in pursuance of his vow) founded the city Bhojakata, and ever afterwards dwelt therein. After the defeat of Rukmin, Krishna married Rukmini in due form, having first made her his own by the Rākshasa ritual. She bore him the gallant Pradyumna, a portion of the deity of love. The demon Sambara carried him off, but he slew the demon.
